questions.question: Who is considered the father of the computer?
questions.explanation: Charles Babbage designed the first mechanical computer, the Analytical Engine.

questions.question: What was the name of the first general-purpose electronic digital computer?
questions.explanation: ENIAC was the first general-purpose electronic digital computer, completed in 1945.

questions.question: Which generation of computers used vacuum tubes?
questions.explanation: First generation computers used vacuum tubes for processing.

questions.question: What replaced vacuum tubes in second generation computers?
questions.explanation: Transistors replaced vacuum tubes in the second generation, making computers smaller and more reliable.

questions.question: Who developed the first compiler?
questions.explanation: Grace Hopper developed the first compiler for a programming language.

questions.question: What does the term 'bug' in computing originally refer to?
options: An actual insect causing a hardware malfunction
questions.explanation: The term originated when an actual moth caused a malfunction in the Harvard Mark II computer.

questions.question: Which company introduced the first personal computer?
questions.explanation: The Altair 8800, made by MITS, is considered the first successful personal computer.

questions.question: What year was the World Wide Web invented?
questions.explanation: Tim Berners-Lee invented the World Wide Web in 1989.

questions.question: Who co-founded Apple Computer?
questions.explanation: Steve Jobs and Steve Wozniak co-founded Apple Computer in 1976.

questions.question: What was the first high-level programming language?
questions.explanation: Fortran, developed in the 1950s, was the first high-level programming language.

questions.question: Which technology defined fourth generation computers?
questions.explanation: Fourth generation computers used microprocessors, putting an entire CPU on a single chip using VLSI.

questions.question: Fifth generation computing is mainly associated with which field?
questions.explanation: Fifth generation systems focus on AI, parallel processing, and natural language understanding.

questions.question: What was the first commercial microprocessor, released in 1971?
questions.explanation: The Intel 4004 was a 4-bit CPU originally designed for a calculator, launching the microprocessor era.

questions.question: Which trio invented the transistor at Bell Labs in 1947?
questions.explanation: William Shockley, John Bardeen, and Walter Brattain shared the 1956 Nobel Prize for the transistor.

questions.question: ARPANET was the direct predecessor of what?
questions.explanation: ARPANET evolved into the Internet; the World Wide Web was built on top of it in 1989.

questions.question: Who invented the computer mouse?
questions.explanation: Douglas Engelbart demonstrated the first mouse, a wooden block with wheels, in 1968's 'Mother of All Demos'.

questions.question: Which 1973 Xerox machine pioneered the graphical user interface?
questions.explanation: The Xerox Alto introduced windows, icons, and a mouse—ideas later adopted by Apple and Microsoft.

questions.question: What was Babbage's earlier calculating machine, designed to tabulate polynomial functions?
questions.explanation: The Difference Engine automated mathematical tables; the later Analytical Engine was fully programmable.

questions.question: Which 1941 machine by Konrad Zuse is considered the first working programmable computer?
questions.explanation: The electromechanical Z3 ran in 1941, predating ENIAC, but was destroyed in WWII bombing.

questions.question: Who sent the first networked email and chose the @ symbol in 1971?
questions.explanation: Ray Tomlinson sent the first ARPANET email and picked @ to separate user from machine name.

questions.question: What was the first widely used graphical web browser, released by NCSA in 1993?
questions.explanation: NCSA Mosaic popularized inline images and point-and-click browsing; its team later founded Netscape.

questions.question: Who coined the term 'artificial intelligence' in 1956?
questions.explanation: John McCarthy coined 'artificial intelligence' for the 1956 Dartmouth conference that founded the field.

questions.question: Which test did Alan Turing propose to judge whether a machine can think?
questions.explanation: The Turing Test deems a machine intelligent if a judge cannot tell its replies from a human's.

questions.question: According to Moore's Law, what roughly doubles about every two years?
questions.explanation: Gordon Moore observed in 1965 that transistor counts per chip doubled roughly every two years.

questions.question: Which 1959 language was designed for business data processing?
questions.explanation: COBOL (Common Business-Oriented Language) used English-like syntax for business applications.

questions.question: What was the first spreadsheet program, a killer app for the Apple II?
questions.explanation: VisiCalc (1979) was the first spreadsheet and a major reason businesses bought Apple II computers.

questions.question: In 1975 a hobbyist bought a mail-order computer kit with front-panel switches that they had to assemble themselves. Which machine did they most likely buy?
questions.explanation: The Altair 8800 was sold as an assemble-it-yourself kit via the January 1975 Popular Electronics cover; the others came fully assembled.

questions.question: Why did second-generation computers run more reliably than first-generation machines?
options: They processed data on punched cards
Transistors replaced bulky, heat-prone vacuum tubes
questions.explanation: Transistors were smaller, cooler, and far more durable than vacuum tubes, slashing failures and machine size.

questions.question: A historian claims the Web and the Internet are the same thing. Which fact corrects them?
options: The Web was invented before the Internet
The Web is a service of linked documents, created in 1989, that runs over the much older Internet
They are simply different spellings of one invention
questions.explanation: The Internet is the underlying packet network dating to ARPANET; Berners-Lee's World Wide Web is one service built on top of it.

questions.question: Which 1981 machine, built from off-the-shelf components, spawned the 'PC-compatible' clone industry that dominated personal computing?
questions.explanation: The IBM PC's open, off-the-shelf design let other manufacturers build compatible clones, standardizing the market.

questions.question: What made the Apple Macintosh's 1984 debut revolutionary for ordinary users?
options: It was the cheapest computer ever sold
It was the first computer to use a keyboard
It brought a graphical interface and mouse to a mass-market machine
It was the first portable computer
questions.explanation: The Macintosh packaged the GUI and mouse, pioneered at Xerox PARC and on the Lisa, into an affordable product for the public.
